docs.title: Klever Docs
docs.text:
Notes, plans, and documentation for Klever Lab projects.

  • K-Suite — open source cloud tools for advanced users: storage wrapper, ingest, egress, and an API-first core.

docs.title: Vision
docs.text: A suite of open source cloud tools designed for advanced technical workloads. The components operate together across cloud environments without requiring monthly software subscriptions.

docs.title: Infrastructure Cost Model
docs.text: Workloads require cloud compute, storage, and network resources. Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) is the primary operating model: users connect credentials from supported cloud providers and pay infrastructure costs directly to those providers.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
• Opinionated provider support: The suite integrates with selected cloud providers that fit the architecture rather than supporting all platforms.
  • Direct provider access: Presets provide standard configurations, while underlying provider options remain directly configurable.
  • Unified interface: The tools present a consistent API and configuration model across disparate cloud services.
  • Workload focus: Architecture and defaults are tuned for specialized, high-throughput, and non-standard technical tasks.

docs.title: Pricing Model
docs.text: The pricing model combines a flat monthly membership fee with direct, at-cost pass-through of underlying cloud provider expenses (storage, compute, bandwidth) or direct BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) provider billing.

docs.title: $5/month — Membership
docs.text:
• Access to all tools.
  • Infrastructure usage billed at direct provider cost for storage, compute, and bandwidth without markups.
  • BYOK where supported: connect external provider accounts to pay providers directly.

docs.title: $10/month — Membership + Hosted Credits
docs.text:
• All features of the $5 tier.
  • An included allowance of usage credits for the hosted deployment run on Klever infrastructure.
  • Credits apply toward compute, storage, and bandwidth consumed on the hosted deployment; subsequent usage is billed at cost.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The software is open source; self-hosting is supported.
  • Hosted credits apply exclusively to the hosted deployment and do not apply to BYOK accounts.
  • Specific credit quotas and unit pass-through rates will be published per tool as each tool reaches general availability.

docs.title: Licensing Notice
docs.text: The software is currently released under an open source license. If infrastructure hosting expenses exceed operating limits, future releases may adopt a source-available or commercial license.

docs.title: API-First Architecture
docs.text:
The API server functions as the central execution layer and authoritative source of state for all tools.

The web application and command-line interfaces operate strictly as clients over this API. External clients can integrate directly against the same endpoints.

docs.title: Cloud Abstraction Layer
docs.text:
The suite operates as an abstraction layer across supported cloud providers.

The architecture provides composable interfaces for cloud primitives while preserving direct access to underlying provider configurations alongside default presets.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A service that executes FFmpeg media transformations in cloud environments on files stored via the storage wrapper.

docs.title: Initial Direction
docs.text: Media processing tasks execute on transient cloud instances equipped with GPU acceleration and high-throughput network access to the storage wrapper, offloading computation and transfer bandwidth from the local client.

docs.title: Core Capabilities
docs.text:
• Select source files managed by the cloud storage wrapper.
  • Execute FFmpeg processing jobs on transient compute instances.
  • Allocate GPU-accelerated instances for hardware encoding and decoding.
  • Leverage high-bandwidth internal networks between compute and storage.
  • Process multi-file batch workloads.

docs.title: Execution Modes
docs.text:
• Guided mode: Standard presets for routine transformations (such as transcoding, scaling, container remuxing, and relocating MP4 moov atoms).
  • Raw mode: Direct execution of arbitrary FFmpeg command strings and multi-step scripts within the worker instance.

docs.title: Execution Lifecycle
docs.text:
The execution model evaluates two designs:

  • Per-job execution: Provision an instance, fetch input files from storage, execute the command, write outputs to storage, and terminate the instance.
  • Interactive session: Maintain an active transient instance for iterative command execution across multiple files.

Evaluation criteria include instance startup latency, compute billing increments, and workflow control requirements.

docs.title: First Milestone
docs.text:
The initial release implements the per-job lifecycle:

  1. Provision a transient compute worker for a single task.
  2. Stage input files from the storage wrapper.
  3. Execute the target FFmpeg command or preset.
  4. Persist output files to the storage wrapper.
  5. Terminate the compute instance.

Interactive sessions are deferred to subsequent releases.

docs.title: Batch Processing
docs.text:
The service will support batch execution over large collections of media assets.

Batch execution must achieve higher cost-efficiency and lower aggregate provisioning overhead than equivalent sequential single-job executions to justify deployment.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A service for uploading and downloading files from cloud object storage with standardized access controls.

docs.title: Initial Direction
docs.text:
The cloud storage wrapper serves as the shared file abstraction layer for the suite. It standardizes object storage credentials, bucket policies, and transfer operations behind a common API.

The API server runs as the authoritative backend. Web and CLI interfaces act as clients over this API, and external integrations can connect directly against the defined endpoints.

docs.title: Core Capabilities
docs.text:
• Upload and download files via standardized endpoints.
  • Apply access control and encryption defaults.
  • Manage provider credentials and bucket configurations.

docs.title: First Milestone
docs.text:
The initial milestone implements a minimal API for authenticated file transfers and directory listings required by downstream services.

Advanced sharing controls, granular role-based permissions, and web-based file management are deferred to subsequent releases. Downstream tools import, export, or mount storage paths directly through this layer.

docs.title: Storage Backends
docs.text:
The storage architecture is built around the S3 API standard.

Target backends:

  • BYOK: Bring Your Own Key for arbitrary S3-compatible endpoints.
  • Backblaze B2 as the default hosted backend, billed at provider cost.
  • rclone integration for additional storage providers (such as Google Drive or Dropbox).

docs.title: Post-POC Capabilities
docs.text:
• Semantic search indexing file contents and metadata attributes.
  • Tagging taxonomies for stored objects and directory paths.
  • Automated semantic profiling to extract descriptive metadata upon object ingestion.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Egress tools distribute content stored in the shared cloud storage layer across various network protocols and applications.

docs.title: Component Services
docs.text:
• Jellyfin server.
  • Secure download links.
  • Encrypted file downloads.
  • Livestreaming with RTMP links.

docs.title: Architecture and Dependencies
docs.text:
Egress tools depend on the cloud storage wrapper as their primary storage backend.

Content is delivered directly from cloud infrastructure to clients without routing data through intermediate user machines. Each egress service operates independently to accommodate differences in protocol handling, compute overhead, and security profiles.

Shared configuration primitives across egress tools include:

  • Source path selectors referencing the cloud storage wrapper.
  • Access policies defining credential requirements and link expiration.
  • Centralized auditing of exposed resources.

docs.title: Distribution Protocols
docs.text:
Distribution mechanisms evaluated for content egress, ordered by architectural complexity:

  • Direct HTTPS links (static, cryptographically signed, or time-limited).
  • Unencrypted HTTP links (requiring explicit configuration).
  • S3 presigned URLs for object storage providers supporting native signing.
  • WebDAV endpoints for file-system navigation.
  • FTP and SFTP file transfer services.
  • Jellyfin media server with on-demand transcoding.
  • RTMP-to-HLS pipelines for live media broadcast.
  • Single-seed BitTorrent transfers for large-file distribution.
  • NNTP/Usenet uploads for Usenet propagation.
  • IPFS for content-addressed peer distribution.

Initial development focuses on the four component services listed above; additional protocols will be evaluated based on operational requirements.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A tool for distributing encrypted files where content confidentiality is preserved independently of link dissemination.

docs.title: Security Model
docs.text:
Protection operates across two distinct layers:

  • Transport security: Downloads are transmitted exclusively over TLS.
  • Payload encryption: Objects are encrypted at rest; storage access alone does not expose plaintext content.

Decryption keys or passphrases are distributed out-of-band.

docs.title: Core Capabilities
docs.text:
• Encrypt files prior to upload or distribution.
  • Generate download URLs associated with client-managed encryption keys.
  • Support both server-side decryption during transfer and client-side zero-knowledge decryption.
  • Avoid logging or persisting encryption keys on backend servers.
  • Apply expiration timestamps and download count thresholds.

docs.title: Storage Integration
docs.text: The tool integrates with the cloud storage wrapper. In zero-knowledge configurations, the storage layer persists only ciphertext, and cryptographic keys remain strictly on client endpoints.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A service for provisioning transient virtual machines with configurable access protocols and automated lifecycle management.

docs.title: Initial Direction
docs.text: Instances support headless environments (SSH) or graphical environments (remote desktop). Resource configurations are selectable to match workload requirements, including compute-optimized, memory-optimized, or cost-optimized instance classes exposed by supported cloud providers.

docs.title: Core Capabilities
docs.text:
• Provision transient virtual machines.
  • Select headless or graphical display environments.
  • Configure CPU, memory, and accelerator allocations.
  • Mount target paths from the cloud storage wrapper.
  • Connect via SSH, WebRTC, or graphical remote desktop protocols.
  • Automated instance teardown upon session completion.

docs.title: Connection Architecture
docs.text:
Connection protocols are integrated as core interfaces:

  • Headless mode: Direct SSH access for command-line execution.
  • Graphical mode: Remote desktop sessions for browser-based or client-based GUI interaction.

The baseline lifecycle covers provisioning, connection handshake, execution, and termination.

docs.title: Storage Integration
docs.text: The VM service mounts directories directly from the cloud storage wrapper via FUSE or network block devices, enabling workloads to operate on shared storage objects with local filesystem semantics.

docs.title: Provider Configuration and Provisioning Latency
docs.text:
The service exposes underlying provider instance specifications alongside pre-configured resource profiles.

To minimize instance provisioning delays, an on-demand pool mode maintains pre-warmed instances, returning connection credentials immediately upon request and absorbing underlying cloud initialization overhead.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Ingest tools transfer external data directly into the shared cloud storage layer.

docs.title: Component Services
docs.text:
• Torrent ingest.
  • Usenet ingest.
  • yt-dlp ingest.

docs.title: Architecture and Execution Model
docs.text:
Ingest tasks execute in cloud compute environments, writing outputs directly to target directories in the cloud storage wrapper without transferring data through client network connections.

Each ingest protocol is managed by a distinct service to handle differences in network protocols, concurrency limits, and state tracking.

Common architectural components include:

  • Shared destination path mapping backed by the cloud storage wrapper.
  • Future network controls for egress IP selection, VPN tunneling, and forward proxy routing.

Network routing controls (VPN, static IP egress, forward proxies) are deferred to subsequent releases.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A service for deploying an ephemeral Jellyfin media server instance connected to directories in the cloud storage wrapper.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Deployment is automated: selecting source media directories provisions and configures an instance without requiring manual server administration.

Instances support transient lifecycles, enabling on-demand provisioning and teardown per viewing session.

docs.title: Core Capabilities
docs.text:
• Automated deployment of pre-configured Jellyfin instances.
  • Mount media libraries from selected cloud storage wrapper directories.
  • Expose web interfaces over TLS via automated DNS or encrypted tunnels.
  • Enforce authenticated user access controls.
  • Teardown and resource release upon session completion.

docs.title: Storage Integration
docs.text: Media directories mount from the shared cloud storage wrapper. Transcoding scratch space streams temporary segments to storage or transient disks rather than requiring persistent local instance storage.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A service for broadcasting media assets stored in cloud storage as live streams via RTMP ingest and HLS delivery.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
The service converts stored media files into live video streams. An RTMP endpoint accepts incoming stream data or initiates playback from storage, and a packaging service segments the stream into HLS playlists delivered over HTTPS.

Stream lifecycles are bound to designated storage sources and support programmatic startup and termination.

docs.title: Core Capabilities
docs.text:
• Expose RTMP ingest endpoints for designated media sources.
  • Package video streams into adaptive HLS segments for multi-client playback.
  • Deliver HLS playlists over TLS endpoints.
  • Apply token-based or IP-restricted viewing controls.
  • Automatic resource teardown upon stream termination.

docs.title: Storage Integration
docs.text: Input media assets are retrieved from the cloud storage wrapper. Manifests and packaged HLS segments can persist back to object storage or remain in transient cache during broadcast.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A service for generating time-limited, cryptographically signed URLs to distribute files from cloud storage.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Access is governed by signed URLs configured with expiration timestamps and capability restrictions.

Permissions are strictly scoped to specific file paths or directory prefixes rather than account-wide access.

docs.title: Core Capabilities
docs.text:
• Generate expiring download URLs for individual files and directories.
  • Cryptographically sign URLs to prevent parameter tampering.
  • Enforce TLS transmission by default, requiring explicit configuration for unencrypted HTTP access.
  • List, revoke, and extend existing download links.
  • Enforce per-link download count limits.

docs.title: Storage Integration
docs.text: URLs resolve against the cloud storage wrapper. Where supported by the underlying provider, native presigned S3 URLs are issued directly. For providers lacking native signing, the service generates authenticated tokens served via an edge gateway.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A service for downloading BitTorrent payloads directly into cloud storage.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: BitTorrent client workers execute in cloud compute instances, assembling payloads and writing completed files directly to target paths in the cloud storage wrapper without transferring data through client network connections.

docs.title: Core Capabilities
docs.text:
• Initiate and manage BitTorrent transfer tasks.
  • Persist completed downloads into designated cloud storage directories.
  • Integrate with the cloud storage wrapper for path resolution and quota tracking.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A service for downloading NNTP/Usenet binaries directly into cloud storage.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: NNTP download workers execute in cloud compute instances, verifying and assembling binaries before writing completed files directly to the cloud storage wrapper without transferring data through client network connections.

docs.title: Core Capabilities
docs.text:
• Initiate and monitor NNTP/NZB download tasks.
  • Verify archive integrity and assemble multi-part binaries.
  • Persist completed files into designated cloud storage directories.
  • Integrate with the cloud storage wrapper for path resolution and quota tracking.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A service that executes yt-dlp media extraction in cloud infrastructure, writing outputs directly into cloud storage.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Media extraction jobs run on cloud compute instances that fetch external audio and video streams and transfer completed files directly into the cloud storage wrapper without intermediate local downloading.

docs.title: Core Capabilities
docs.text:
• Execute yt-dlp extraction tasks on cloud compute workers.
  • Persist extracted media and metadata to designated cloud storage directories.
  • Integrate with the cloud storage wrapper for path resolution and quota tracking.
